description: Short-lived candidate queue for Woods Run X replies. Pending candidates expire after 72 hours.

candidates.why_match: A lumber-industry consultant shared a current macroeconomic piece with a forestry-products audience; Woods Run's same-week diesel/lumber divergence adds a concrete sector-specific operating read.
candidates.woods_run_item: U.S. diesel reached $6.285/gal, up 31.8 cents in a week, while November lumber fell 7.2% to $537/MBF.
candidates.draft_reply: One forestry-sector datapoint that makes the macro squeeze tangible: U.S. diesel hit $6.285/gal, up 31.8¢ in a week, while November lumber fell 7.2% to $537/MBF. Higher operating costs and a weaker product-price signal are arriving together.

candidates.why_match: COFI's post argues for the community importance of a strong B.C. forest sector; Woods Run has a specific current stumpage/price contrast that adds operating economics rather than generic agreement.
candidates.woods_run_item: B.C. forecast average Crown stumpage at C$13.55/m³, 11% below its February assumption, while raising its SPF 2x4 lumber-price assumption.
candidates.draft_reply: B.C. cut its expected Crown stumpage to C$13.55/m³, 11% below its February assumption, even while lifting its SPF 2x4 price assumption. A good illustration of why headline lumber prices and forest economics can diverge.

candidates.display_name: Arizona Department of Forestry and Fire Management
candidates.why_match: The post is directly about the Sunflower restoration work; the newest Woods Run issue adds the unusually useful scale, financing and timber-volume details. The post is slightly older than the normal window but the development is newly relevant and still active.
candidates.woods_run_item: Kaibab GNA work covers nearly 14,000 acres, is expected to produce about 36 MMBF, and combines $6.4M in federal funding with a dollar-for-dollar Salt River Project match and reinvested timber-sale revenue.
candidates.draft_reply: The scale is notable: the first Kaibab GNA push covers nearly 14,000 acres and is expected to produce about 36 MMBF. With $6.4M in federal funding matched by SRP and sale revenue reinvested, commercial timber is helping finance the restoration loop.
